title: Leverage Points Framework — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Leverage Points Framework's rich face, its first round, at Sketch tier, a proposal, remade after the challenge. One small stock-and-flow model of a creator's practice runs both pieces. One tests the core insight the page's way, the goal switched rather than nudged, against a parameter pushed across its whole range, and shows the dial reading failing beside it. The other puts a fast signal beside a slow one, scores who steers, and tries the page's temporal discipline with views at half weight and with views demoted. Every number is this model's. I grow when Loudon answers the offers, and I never hold the entry's words.
grain: The page's own ## grain. Two sections carry one piece each. The 12 Leverage Points is one ## with seven ### under it, so its one piece (on #9, Delays) carries one stamp and one all-or-nothing approval for all twelve points; it sits beside the #9–#7 paragraph. The opening section, Application Framework, Why the Platform Wants You at #12, The Meta-Leverage of This Framework and Cross-Domain Resonance carry none: the bundle had no proofs or media to gather, and no claim in them was one a piece could test without inventing the page's numbers. The sibling page's self-diagnostic (Projects/Meadows and an Artist's Career) was read as prior art and not gathered; it tallies a person's decisions and tests nothing here.

offers.what: Read as the page reads it, a change in kind (#3 "isn't a parameter change", #2 "a click of the mind"), the opportunity line holds in this model: switching the goal so views leave what the creator steers by moved the stocks D 1.5 or more in 59 of 64 draws and 0.50 or less in none, 2.46 at the defaults against 0.50 for a parameter pushed to the end of its range. Only a reading the page does not make fails, the goal nudged like a dial (beaten by the parameter in 64 of 64). For Loudon, optional: the opportunity line could name the change in kind ("a small effort that changes what the system aims at"), which #3 already says; declining it loses nothing. Whether a whole change of goal is a small effort, the model cannot say. This model's numbers.

#9, Delays. The hijack reproduces in this model: equal weights, daily looks, 99.9% of decisions follow views and 50.3% the slow signal; it holds with no delay too (99.9% / 49.2%), so in this model it comes from timescale, not lag. Looking less often with views still at half weight does not lift it (0 of 64 draws). With views demoted to 1% of what the creator reflects on, weekly looks lift the capture in 64 of 64 draws against 16 of 64 daily, and raise K more than 10% in 63. For Loudon: the #9 paragraph could say temporal discipline frees the slow signal when the metric is also demoted in what you reflect on; "no daily metric checking" is the nearest phrase, and the edit sharpens it more than it reverses it. This model's numbers.

verdicts.why: It tests a reading the page does not make (the goal as a dial nudged by a share of its range) and headlines it as 'the core insight fails', while its own after-step confirms the page's reading (switch D 2.46 vs 0.50); retitle the verdict to what was tested, say the parameter's D per effort is fixed by construction, and fix the explanation, which is views' direct gain on the promotion share, not the delay (Ds = 0 here) or chiefly the lottery (sigma 0.01: goal nudge D 0.000).

pieces.title: same effort, three places · a stock-and-flow test
pieces.caption: **Does a high leverage point move more than a parameter?** Starts with one stock (Meadows' bathtub), then four, then a creator who steers by what they watch. The test reads the page its own way: the goal switched, views out of what the creator steers by, against a parameter pushed across its whole range, with the rule written before the 64 draws. It holds in this model (D at least 1.5 in 59 of 64 draws, at most 0.50 in none; 2.46 against 0.50 at the defaults). Beside it, the model's own dial reading, the goal nudged by 10% or 25% of its range, does nothing: the parameter beats it in all 64 draws, and the parameter's number is fixed by how the model is built. The piece says why: views answer posting the same day. Every number is this model's. No sound.

pieces.title: who is steering · #9 Delays, as a controller
pieces.caption: **Does fast feedback capture the creator, and does temporal discipline free them?** Starts with a creator steering by one slow signal, then through a delay, then with noisy daily views beside it. A meter asks which signal each decision followed, against a chance level of 50%. The hijack rule comes before the first trial. The page's situation is hijacked: 99.9% of decisions follow views and 50.3% the slow signal, and it stays hijacked with no delay at all (99.9% against 49.2%). With views at half weight, looking less often does not lift the capture (0 of 64 draws). With views demoted to 1%, weekly looks lift it in 64 of 64 draws against 16 daily. The same model as the core insight's piece. Every number is this model's. No sound.
